questions.q: What is the difference between a debug log category and a log level?
options: A category is a distinct area of execution (like Apex_Code or Database); a log level (like DEBUG or FINEST) controls how much detail that category records
They are the same thing with two different names
Log levels apply only to triggers, while categories apply only to classes
Categories are set per org, while log levels are set per method
questions.explain: A category identifies what kind of execution is being tracked, while the log level assigned to that category controls the verbosity of what gets recorded for it.

questions.q: What is a Trace Flag used for?
options: Marking a line of code to be deleted before deployment
Flagging a record for manual review in a list view
Capturing debug logs for a specific user's actions over a specific time window, including actions outside Execute Anonymous
Enabling field-level security on a specific field
questions.explain: A Trace Flag configures debug log capture for a chosen user and time window, which is how you capture a log from a real UI action, Flow, or scheduled job rather than just an anonymous Apex run.

questions.q: What line tag identifies the output of a `System.debug()` call inside a debug log?
options: SYSTEM_OUTPUT
DEBUG_LOG
APEX_TRACE
USER_DEBUG
questions.explain: Every System.debug() call produces a USER_DEBUG line in the log, which is what you filter to when scanning a log for your own debug output.

questions.q: Why might setting every log category to FINEST make a debugging session harder, not easier?
options: FINEST is not a valid log level in Apex
It captures the maximum detail across every category at once, producing a much larger, noisier log that's harder to scan for the specific thing you're looking for
FINEST disables System.debug() output entirely
FINEST can only be used by System Administrators
questions.explain: Maximum verbosity across every category produces a large, noisy log; the practical approach is raising only the categories actually relevant to the problem at hand.

questions.q: Why is `System.debug('ContactLeadSourceCleanupBatch.execute result count: ' + scope.size());` considered a better habit than `System.debug(scope.size());`?
options: Adding context labels makes the log line much easier to recognize and search later, especially once a method has several debug statements
The first version runs faster at execution time
Apex requires a String literal before every debug value
There is no real difference between the two
questions.explain: A labeled debug statement is far easier to find and interpret later than a bare value, especially in a log with many debug lines from different parts of the code.
